title: Function-call termination normalization discrepancy causing duplicated/truncated evals for strategic customer
creator: Diego Ramos
description: High-severity customer report: after recent serving runtime changes (sampling default harmonization + stop-token normalization), a strategic enterprise customer observed duplicated blocks and truncated values in eval outputs for prompts that use nested function-calling markers. Issue reproduces only when requests route through Dedicated pools with Private routing overlay and when the model uses function-calling delimiters ("<CALL_START>" / "<CALL_END>"). The customer uses deterministic evals for automated scoring; regression caused ~12% drop in their eval pass rate and triggered an SL escalation.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use customer eval harness with function-calling prompts that include explicit call boundary tokens.
2) Route request via dedicated pool + private overlay (customer's config: private-routing: true, fallback: true).
3) Use sampling defaults: top_p=0.0, temperature=0.0 (deterministic), and runtime global stop normalization enabled.
4) Observe duplicated call-body insertion in output or early truncation at call-end when KV cache hits and batching occurs.
root_cause: A normalization pass in the routing layer was introduced to canonicalize stop sequences across hosted/dedicated/private paths. That pass incorrectly de-escaped function-call boundary markers for routed requests only, and a separate KV-cache path assumed canonical markers were already escaped. When batching combined a canonicalized request with cached prefix entries, the runtime double-applied termination semantics, producing duplicated call bodies or cutting generation at the wrong offset. Sampling default harmonization (making deterministic defaults explicit) changed timing and increased batching probability, surfacing the bug.
mitigation: Hotfix: add a guarded idempotent normalization routine that detects already-normalized markers (feature gate: routing.termination.idempotent=true).
Customer mitigation: instruct customer to set routing strict_stop=true for affected eval jobs (temporary workaround).
Operational: add Datadog alert for spike in repeated token patterns and sudden eval pass-rate drops for customer-specific project tags.
resolution_plan: 1) Backport idempotent normalization hotfix to runtime branches (PR: runtime/#1842) and push asap to staging dedicated pools.
2) Run full regression suite using customer's eval harness in both Private and Dedicated environments; include sampling-default permutations.
3) Add unit tests for function-call marker escaping + KV cache interaction and an integration test that simulates batching with cached prefixes.
4) Postmortem and customer-facing root-cause write-up; offer remediation credit and consult to update their eval harness for stricter stop configuration.
5) Plan follow-up: review other normalization passes in routing and create a policy doc describing canonical token ownership (routing vs runtime vs client).
progress_updates: 2026-03-04: Initial report from Customer Success (CS) after customer run of nightly evals. Triage assigned to ENG. Diego owned initial investigation.
2026-03-05: Reproduced locally with customer corpus when routing through dedicated pool; observed duplication pattern. Created temporary alert dashboard (Datadog).
2026-03-06: Narrowed to normalization pass in routing layer and KV-cache interaction. Implemented prototype idempotent normalization; initial tests pass.
2026-03-10: Security review not required; engaged infra to schedule hotfix rollout to staging dedicated pools. Customer provided additional logs and their eval harness (shared Google Drive link).
2026-03-12: Submitted PR runtime/#1842 (unit + integration tests). Running canary in one dedicated private pool; monitoring for regressions.
2026-03-13: Canary looks stable; duplication metric dropped to baseline in canary pool. Preparing customer patch window and communications.
notes_for_support: Advise customer to set routing.strict_stop=true for affected evals as an immediate mitigation.
Schedule a joint run with customer engineering during patch window to validate 1:1 parity with their harness.
Offer 1 week of elevated monitoring and SLA credit for the impacted eval jobs.
